text: At 87 minutes, Seabrook Town assert tactical control by exploiting their 3-4-3 formation’s wide crossing approach, generating 5 final third entries and achieving a field tilt of 52% over the last 8 minutes to intensify pressure on Harbour City’s 4-2-3-1 setup. Their pressing trigger is evident in a higher PPDA of 4.8 compared to Harbour City’s 4.3, enabling quicker ball recoveries in advanced positions and facilitating rapid transitions that contributed to two shots with a combined xG of 0.15—including Kian Romano’s off-target header at 85’ [#1744]. This systemic overload of wide channels disrupts Harbour City’s patient short passing rhythm, resulting in increased high turnovers (2 vs. Harbour’s 1) and allowing Seabrook to dominate attacking momentum despite inferior overall possession (46.4%) and pass accuracy (67.9%). The mechanism of sustained wide pressure combined with aggressive pressing triggers a phase where Seabrook Town controls the match tempo and creates promising offensive opportunities.
